# From experimental data to reproducible analysis and editable scientific figures

<p class="hero-byline">Benjamín Szenfeld · BIOSZEN 2.1.1 · August 2026</p>

**BIOSZEN** is an open-source R package with a modular Shiny application for biological data analysis and visualization. It helps researchers turn Excel tables, CSV files, and optical-density time series into statistical results, growth parameters, customizable plots, and reproducible exports without requiring plotting code.

[Install](https://bioszen.r-universe.dev/){.button .button-primary}
[Try online](https://bioszen-test.share.connect.posit.cloud){.button .button-secondary}
[Manual](https://github.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/blob/main/inst/app/www/MANUAL_EN.md){.button .button-secondary}
[GitHub](https://github.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN){.button .button-secondary}
:::

## One workflow, from input to communication

BIOSZEN brings data preparation, exploratory visualization, statistical analysis, growth-curve analysis, figure assembly, and reproducibility records into one guided local workflow.

- **Accessible analysis:** work through a graphical interface while retaining scriptable R functions for repeatable pipelines.
- **Biological statistics:** use control-based normalization, replicate-aware quality control, normality tests, significance tests, post hoc comparisons, and multiple-testing correction.
- **Scientific figures:** create boxplots, bar plots, violin plots, curves, stacked plots, heatmaps, correlation plots, and correlation matrices.
- **Reproducible outputs:** export processed data, statistics, metadata, plots, composition panels, and reusable ZIP bundles.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/app/01_app_home_overview.png){fig-alt="BIOSZEN application overview" .screenshot}

## Who is BIOSZEN for?

Experimental biologists, microbiologists, students, and research teams that want guided biological data analysis with reproducible R workflows and publication-ready outputs.

## Install and launch

BIOSZEN is available from R-universe and requires R 4.1 or later.

```r
install.packages(
  "BIOSZEN",
  repos = c(
    "https://bioszen.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)

BIOSZEN::BIOSZEN()
```

After restarting RStudio, BIOSZEN can also be opened from **Addins > Launch BIOSZEN in Browser**.

The installed application runs locally: files loaded into the local session are processed on the user's computer. The [limited online demo](https://bioszen-test.share.connect.posit.cloud) is useful for exploring the interface; use the local installation for the complete workflow and for sensitive experimental data.

## Complete analysis workflow

1. **Prepare:** use a Platemap + Curves workbook structure, grouped parameters, summary tables, or CSV input.
2. **Load:** import the primary experimental file and, when needed, the well-based time series.
3. **Inspect:** validate groups, parameters, replicates, and well mappings before analysis.
4. **Visualize:** choose a plot family and configure labels, axes, fonts, colors, legends, and annotations.
5. **Analyze:** normalize against controls, run statistical tests, and inspect significance results.
6. **Export:** save plots, tables, metadata, PowerPoint figures, and reproducibility bundles.

### Prepare and validate the experiment

The recommended workflow uses a **Platemap + Curves** structure. The primary workbook contains a `Datos` sheet with experimental observations and a `PlotSettings` sheet describing plotting metadata. A separate curves file contains a `Time` column and well-based measurements such as `A1`, `A2`, and `A3`.

BIOSZEN also supports grouped-parameter workbooks, summary inputs containing mean, standard deviation, and sample size, and CSV input for larger datasets. Example files and templates are included in the repository.

For plate-based experiments, the values in the `Well` column must correspond to the curve column names.

### Filter, visualize, and compare

Users can select groups, media or conditions, parameters, and replicates. Biological and technical replicate information can support manual quality control and reproducibility-oriented filtering.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/app/03_filter_media_conditions.png){fig-alt="Filtering experimental conditions in BIOSZEN" .screenshot}

Plot settings include labels, axes, fonts, colors, legends, annotations, dimensions, and output resolution.

::: {.gallery}
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/plots/01_Boxplot.png){fig-alt="Boxplot generated by BIOSZEN"}
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/plots/05_stacked.png){fig-alt="Stacked plot generated by BIOSZEN"}
:::

### Normalize and run statistical analyses

BIOSZEN supports control-based normalization while retaining replicate-aware behavior. It provides Shapiro-Wilk, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, and Anderson-Darling normality tests. Depending on the design and data structure, users can run ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Student's t-test, or Wilcoxon tests, together with post hoc comparisons and multiple-testing correction using Holm, FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg), Bonferroni, or no correction.

Significance results can be reviewed as tables and incorporated into supported plot types.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/app/09_significance_tests_setup.png){fig-alt="Statistical test configuration in BIOSZEN" .screenshot}

## Analyze microbial growth curves

The growth module plots optical-density trajectories and extracts biologically useful parameters for each well or curve. BIOSZEN first applies its robust exponential-phase detector and uses the permissive detector only to complete values that the robust method could not estimate.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioszen/BIOSZEN/main/Gallery/screenshots/app/13_growth_parameters_workflow.png){fig-alt="BIOSZEN growth parameter workflow" .screenshot}

```r
growth_results <- BIOSZEN::growth_parameters(
  "Curvas.xlsx",
  max_time = 48,
  time_interval = 0.5,
  output_dir = "growth_results",
  overwrite = FALSE
)
```

| Parameter | What it represents | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `µMax` | Maximum specific growth rate estimated during the detected exponential-growth interval. | Higher values indicate faster exponential growth; units are inverse time. |
| `max_percap_time` | Mean time of the interval used to estimate `µMax`. | Locates the strongest exponential-growth interval on the time axis. |
| `doub_time` | Estimated doubling time, calculated as `log(2) / µMax`. | Lower values indicate faster growth. |
| `lag_time` | Estimated start of the detected exponential phase. | Larger values indicate a longer delay before rapid growth. |
| `ODmax` | Highest observed optical-density value. | Maximum recorded density during the experiment. |
| `max_time` | First time at which `ODmax` is observed. | Indicates when the maximum recorded density is reached. |
| `AUC` | Area under the complete OD-versus-time curve. | Summarizes accumulated growth across the experiment. |
| `OD0` | First valid measurement after observations are ordered by time. | Describes starting density or baseline OD. |

Time-related parameters inherit the unit used in the input `Time` column.

## Export publication-ready results

Individual plots and multi-plot composition panels can be exported for analysis records, manuscripts, posters, presentations, and reports. BIOSZEN supports PNG, PDF, processed Excel workbooks, statistical tables, metadata, ZIP bundles, and PowerPoint files.

## Preserve and reuse the analysis

Once the analysis is configured, users can export its metadata and create a ZIP bundle containing the relevant outputs. Metadata can later be imported to restore the analysis state and reproduce the figure-generation workflow.

The app is the primary interactive interface, while exported package commands support scripts and automated pipelines:

```r
# Launch BIOSZEN
BIOSZEN::BIOSZEN()

# Extract growth parameters
results <- BIOSZEN::growth_parameters("Curvas.xlsx")

# Check for and install an approved update
BIOSZEN::bioszen_update_available()
BIOSZEN::bioszen_update()

# Display the official citation
BIOSZEN::bioszen_citation()
```
